problems.title: The Reuleaux tetrahedron does not have constant width
problems.statement_md: Take regular tetrahedron vertices $(a,a,a),(a,-a,-a),(-a,a,-a),(-a,-a,a)$ with $a=1/(2\sqrt2)$, and intersect their unit balls. Exhibit two points of the intersection at distance $\sqrt3-1/\sqrt2>1$, even though its width in a vertex-to-opposite-face direction is one.
problems.hint_md: Look for the two exceptional points on the horizontal coordinate axis, equidistant from the relevant pairs of tetrahedral vertices.

problems.title: Helper midpoints for a dual edge pair
problems.statement_md: Four points satisfy $|a-c|=|a-d|=|b-c|=|b-d|=1$, $|a-b|=2u$, $|c-d|=2v$, with $0<u,v\leq1/2$. Show that, up to a rigid motion, they have coordinates $a=(0,0,-u)$, $b=(0,0,u)$, $c=(-v,h,0)$, $d=(v,h,0)$, $h=\sqrt{1-u^2-v^2}$. Use the edge midpoints as helper points.
problems.hint_md: Place the midpoint of $ab$ at the origin. Points equidistant from $a,b$ lie in its perpendicular bisector plane; then use the midpoint of chord $cd$.

sources.locator: Section Dual spindle–wedge cells, opening coordinate construction

figures.caption_md: The midpoints O and H reduce the four cross-distance constraints to h²+u²+v²=1.
figures.alt: Three-dimensional diagram of two perpendicular opposite edges, their midpoints, and four dashed unit cross edges.

problems.title: A dihedral angle from two helper triangles
problems.statement_md: Let $|a-c|=|a-d|=|b-c|=|b-d|=1$, $|a-b|=2u$, $|c-d|=2v$, with $0<u,v\leq1/2$. Put $s=2\arcsin u$ and $t=2\arcsin v$. Let $\phi_{ab}$ be the angle between the half-planes $abc$ and $abd$ about the line $ab$ toward $c,d$. Prove $\phi_{ab}=2\arcsin(v/\sqrt{1-u^2})$ and derive the analogous formula for $\phi_{cd}$.
problems.hint_md: Cut perpendicular to the edge axis through its midpoint. The opening angle becomes the vertex angle of an isosceles triangle.

problems.title: Area of a spindle patch by a one-dimensional integral
problems.statement_md: Let $0<\theta\leq\pi/3$ and $0<\phi\leq2\pi$. All angles are in radians. Rotate $y(x)=\sqrt{1-x^2}-\cos(\theta/2)$, for $|x|\leq\sin(\theta/2)$, through an angle $\phi$ about the $x$-axis. Prove that the area of the curved surface is $2\phi[\sin(\theta/2)-(\theta/2)\cos(\theta/2)]$.
problems.hint_md: Write a surface-of-revolution parametrization. The factor $\sqrt{1+y\prime(x)^2}$ cancels part of the square root in the profile.

figures.caption_md: Rotate the minor arc AB around its chord; the distance from C to the chord is cos(θ/2).
figures.alt: Unit circle center below a horizontal chord, with two unit radii and the central angle marked.

problems.title: Spherical face area by an auxiliary interior point
problems.statement_md: A convex geodesic polygon lies in an open hemisphere of the unit sphere and has cyclic vertices $v_1,\ldots,v_m$. Choose an interior unit point $q$. Using the solid-angle identity $E(a,b,c)=2\operatorname{atan2}(\det(a,b,c),1+a\cdot b+b\cdot c+c\cdot a)$ for an oriented spherical triangle, prove an area formula for the polygon and show it is independent of $q$. Explain how to handle a spherical face on a sphere centered at $p$.
problems.hint_md: Join the helper point to each boundary vertex by a minor geodesic. Sum the oriented triangle areas rather than averaging them.

sources.locator: Auxiliary-point triangulation of the geodesic face decomposition in Volume_Meissner.tex §3

figures.caption_md: An auxiliary interior point divides the spherical octant into three geodesic triangles.
figures.alt: Spherical octant with its three coordinate-axis vertices and geodesic spokes from an interior helper point.

problems.title: Exact volume of either Meissner tetrahedron
problems.statement_md: You may use the Meissner surface-area formula $S=2\pi-2\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}f(s_i,t_i)$ for unit width, where $f(s,t)=t\cos(t/2)\arcsin(\sin(s/2)/\cos(t/2))$. Compute the area and volume for either Meissner tetrahedron, whose three dual pairs all have $s_i=t_i=\pi/3$.
problems.hint_md: All three summands coincide. Relate $\arcsin(1/\sqrt3)$ to $\arccos(1/3)$ by a half-angle identity, then apply Blaschke’s relation.

figures.caption_md: Spherical patches are blue, wedges pale green, and spindle patches orange. Both choices have the same exact area and volume. Triangulated illustrations.
figures.alt: Side-by-side rendered Meissner tetrahedra with the star and face choices of smoothed edges.

problems.title: Convexity and superadditivity of an edge contribution
problems.statement_md: For $f(s,t)=t\cos(t/2)\arcsin(\sin(s/2)/\cos(t/2))$ on $[0,\pi/3]^2$, prove $f(0,t)=0$, $f(s,t)\geq st/2$, and, for $a,b\geq0$ with $a+b\leq\pi/3$, $f(a,t)+f(b,t)\leq f(a+b,t)$.
problems.hint_md: With $t$ fixed, compute the first two derivatives with respect to $s$. Convexity together with a zero value at the origin gives the splitting inequality.

sources.locator: Appendix A, first-variable derivatives; superadditivity derived here

problems.title: Counting the diameters added by helper points
problems.statement_md: A finite unit-diameter set $X\subset\mathbb R^3$ is called extremal when it has $2|X|-2$ unit-distance pairs. Suppose $Y\subsetneq X$ is also extremal, $Z=X\setminus Y$ has $k$ points, and $q$ of the unit-distance pairs have both endpoints in $Z$. Prove that exactly $2k$ new pairs appear and that $\sum_{z\in Z}\deg_X(z)=2k+q$. If every vertex of $X$ has degree at least three, prove $k\geq3$ and characterize $k=3$.
problems.hint_md: Subtract the extremal pair counts. In the degree sum over the new points, internal pairs are counted twice and crossing pairs once.

problems.title: Deleting a degree-two point preserves extremality
problems.statement_md: Let $X$ be an extremal unit-diameter set in $\mathbb R^3$ with at least five points. Show that deleting a point of degree two leaves an extremal unit-diameter set. Explain why this counting argument alone does not compare the volumes of the corresponding Meissner bodies.
problems.hint_md: Count how many unit-distance pairs disappear. Then distinguish information about the graph from information about geometric area contributions.

problems.title: Why a tetrahedron has two smoothing types
problems.statement_md: Choose one edge from each of the three pairs of opposite edges of a tetrahedron. Prove that the three chosen edges form either a vertex star or a triangular face. Count the choices of each type.
problems.hint_md: View the selected edges as a graph on four vertices. If no vertex has degree three, rule out a three-edge path using the opposite-edge restriction.
